reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of SPTD lies in leveraging training dynamics to generate an abstention signal without retraining. By sampling model checkpoints during training, one can compute prediction disagreement as a proxy for uncertainty. This is mathematically grounded in the idea that models with high instability across checkpoints are less confident in their predictions. The finite-sample gap decomposition provides a structured way to analyze how much performance degrades relative to an ideal oracle, breaking it down into components such as Bayes risk, approximation error, ranking error, statistical fluctuations, and miscellaneous errors. These components help prioritize improvements in reliability. The Mirage adversarial audit addresses potential abuse of uncertainty signals by modeling adversarial manipulation and proposing audit mechanisms. Together, these primitives form a coherent framework for trustworthy deployment of ML models in GSE’s pick-abstention pipeline.
